newsitem.title: USA: MCI says FCC rule does not go far enough.
newsitem.headline: MCI says FCC rule does not go far enough.

text.p: MCI Communications Corp said Wednesday the decision by the U.S. Federal Communications Commission to overhaul the nation's phone access charges is a first step but does not go far enough.

"Today's announcement by the Federal Communications Commission of an immediate $1.7 billion net reduction in interstate access charges is a first step towards eliminating the billions of dollars of unjustified overcharges by the local monopoly phone companies," said Timothy Price, MCI's president and chief operating officer.
"Much more needs to be done. The FCC and the states must now examine and eliminate the remaining overcharges," he said in a company statement.
MCI said it will continue to fight at federal and state levels for lower access charges.

"MCI is disappointed that the FCC's plan raises telephone costs to some residential and business consumers," Price said. "The better course is to eliminate the unnecessary subsidies now buried in access revenues and deliver lower prices to all customers."
The FCC said earlier today that it decided on an up-front reduction of long-distance access charges of $1.7 billion and $18.5 billion over five years.
The ruling is meant to keep basic residential phone rates at their current levels and to lower the rates of business and residential customers who make lots of long-distance calls.
Customers with more than one phone line and who make few long-distance calls could see their phone costs rise.
